A1.justification: Both PDFs are readable versions of the same DMSG research, with matching methods, benchmarks and main results despite the changed title. The supplied v1 ends at its references despite appendix cross-references; v2 includes Appendix A.1–A.7. Their reported content supports reliable comparison.

before.justification: Section 4 reports original DMSG classification results, continual-learning trajectories and replay-component ablations across four graph datasets.

after.justification: v2 retains those original experiments and additionally reports buffer-selection comparisons and buffer-size sensitivity results in Appendix A.6.

M1.justification: Algorithm 1 and the method objectives retain the greedy diversity selector, variational replay, adversarial discriminator, graph reconstruction and gradient-reversal optimization. Appendix A.4 supplies explicit update equations without establishing a changed underlying procedure.

E1.justification: Both evaluate class-incremental node classification on CoraFull, OGB-Arxiv, Reddit and OGB-Products, with 35, 20, 20 and 23 tasks respectively. The additional analyses use this retained coverage.

E2.justification: Table 1 adds SSM and SEM comparison rows absent from v1's table, although v1 already contains SEM-labelled comparisons in Figures 3–4. Appendix Table 4 additionally compares DMS with K-center, Coverage Maximization and Mean of Feature within the DMSG framework, substantially expanding the reported comparisons.

E3.justification: The new analyses introduce controlled selector substitutions and buffer-size sweeps: 40–80 for CoraFull and 200–600 for the other datasets. Existing AA/AF metrics and stated backbone settings remain unchanged. Appendix A.5's additional training settings are disclosures, not evidence that the original experiments changed.

E4.justification: Appendix A.6 adds direct tests of buffer-selection effectiveness and sensitivity to memory capacity across all four datasets. It also extends task-level accuracy-matrix analysis to Reddit and OGB-Products. The original replay-loss ablations and CoraFull/OGB-Arxiv matrices are retained.

E5.justification: Appendix A.6.3 explicitly discusses standard deviations for the buffer-size study, whereas v1 leaves its numerical ± reporting and shaded curves unexplained. This adds limited uncertainty information; neither version specifies repeated-run counts, seeds, confidence intervals or significance-testing procedures.

E6.justification: Shared Table 1 rows, Table 2 and Figures 3–4 retain their results; DMSG's AA values remain 77.8, 50.7, 98.1 and 66.0. v2 adds SSM/SEM AA and AF entries, alternative-selector scores, buffer-size curves and additional accuracy matrices. These expand the evidence without demonstrating improved performance of the retained method.

T1.justification: Appendix A.1 adds a chi-square/Wishart argument about buffer covariance; A.2 supplies the greedy approximation argument and monotonicity/submodularity lemmas; A.3 derives the reconstruction ELBO and Gaussian KL expression. v1 states the main bounds and references supporting material absent from its supplied PDF.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction and conclusion retain the same principal contributions: diversified intra/inter-class memory selection, generative replay and superior graph incremental-learning performance. Retitling the paper around continuous model reuse does not redefine these claims.

C2.justification: Appendix A.6 adds interpretations about compatibility with alternative selectors, robustness across buffer sizes and possible noise from larger buffers. Existing explanations of forgetting and the limitation concerning the unchanged graph feature extractor remain. The new CM/MF improvement interpretation is broader than Tables 1 and 4 consistently support.

D1.justification: Appendix A.5 newly documents class ordering, two classes per task, 60/20/20 splits, buffer sizes of 60 or 400, 200 training epochs, learning rate and weight decay of 0.001, and loss weights [1,20,1,1]. It also describes baseline backbone selection and result provenance. The abstract adds a code/data repository link, whose availability is not independently verified.

R1.justification: Section 5 and Appendix A.7 add recent graph continual-learning references and discussion, including PUMA and task-incremental inference assumptions. Additional citations support datasets, baselines and theoretical exposition. The central positioning around diversified memory remains, and most earlier related-work discussion is retained after relocation.

P1.justification: v2 changes the title, author information and publication header, makes localized wording and cross-reference corrections, and replaces the lengthy main-text related-work subsections with a shorter Section 5 plus Appendix A.7. Most existing methodological and experimental prose remains substantially intact.

P2.justification: v2 redraws the framework diagram, relocates Figure 1, expands Table 1 and adopts conference formatting. It adds dataset-growth plots and statistics, further accuracy matrices, a selector-comparison table and buffer-size plots in Figures 5–7 and Tables 3–4. These substantially expand the visual presentation.

improvement.justification: v2 substantially improves reproducibility and empirical scrutiny by supplying previously missing experimental details, explicit strong-baseline comparisons and direct tests of selection strategy and memory capacity. These address important gaps in evaluating v1's contributions. The new greedy proof still assumes that inter-class gains outweigh intra-class losses without establishing this, and the CM/MF improvement narrative overgeneralizes the tables. Those weaknesses limit the added arguments, but the gains in documented settings and targeted empirical evidence remain substantial.
